description: Does a cosine learning-rate decay make a run's result consistent enough that replicates stop being necessary? A constant rate takes full-size steps long after the fit has arrived, which is what a run wandering inside a wide band at its end looks like, so decaying to zero should narrow that band almost by construction. The question this panel actually has to answer is the SECOND one: whether the RESULT is more consistent between runs, which is what decides whether a comparison still needs more than one seed. THE HELD-ASIDE DRAW IS PINNED ACROSS EVERY ARM (split_seed 0) while the initialization seed varies, because a seed normally moves both and the difference between two runs' scores would otherwise mix a different fit with different rows scored — the arms here are scored on exactly the same rows, so what separates them is the fit alone. Three initializations per schedule. A narrower within-run band is not on its own a reason to drop replicates: it is the between-run spread of the final result that a paired contrast is read against, and a schedule that buys consistency by settling into a worse fit has bought nothing, so the level is reported beside the spreads. THE PANEL RUNS BOTH HOLDOUT UNITS, and the problem arms are the ones the LEVEL has to be judged on. A held-out ROW is one more attempt by a user whose ability was fitted and on a problem whose parameters were, so that score keeps improving for as long as the fit keeps sharpening on material it has already seen — and a schedule that decays to zero stops exactly that. Judged on rows alone, any decay therefore looks costly whether or not it gave up anything that generalizes. Whole held-out problems are the unit that can tell those apart, so the row arms speak to the within-run band and the problem arms decide whether the decay costs accuracy.
